Rajiv —

Thanks, great set of questions. I attached a simple workbook (tiering-scenarios-workbook.xlsx) with three scenarios you can tweak: baseline (no quant), aggressive quant (4-bit), and int8. The sheet includes:

- token-level unit cost estimates
- assumptions for batch size, cache hit rate (prefix/KV), and avg latency impact per configuration
- a computed P&L for the committed discount bands

Quick answers up front:
- 4-bit quant often yields ~1.8–2.5x improvement in tokens/sec vs fp16 depending on kernel availability; int8 is usually cleaner but model-dependent. For your median 350-token chat, 4-bit should reduce per-token GPU cost by ~35–50% in our tests; int8 tends to be ~25–40% depending on exact model and sequence lengths.
- To hit a 20% effective unit cost reduction at the platform level, realistic operational assumptions are: batching to avg 6–8 requests per batch for generative endpoints and a cache hit of 25–30% across repeat prefixes. The workbook shows breakpoints.
- Latency: at p95 you should be able to stay below 300ms if you keep batching conservative (<=8) and enable async streaming; heavy batching (>12) increases p95 notably for shorter sequences. Also consider prefix caching of embeddings/KB responses to avoid re-generation.

Aditya — can you add a short note in the attached PDF (quant-recommendation-notes.pdf) summarizing recommended runtime knobs for their fleet (kernel selection, KV cache sizing, batch cap)? Marissa — can you confirm what discount bands we want to commit for a 12-month contract and whether we can offer phased rollouts (sample pilot credits, then bumped commit after Q2)?

Rajiv — quick technical note from runtime side, summary:

- Kernel selection: prefer models with Triton/TVM optimized kernels for your target GPU; those show the biggest win with 4-bit. If we onboard a custom variant (pruned or LoRA), we should re-benchmark.
- Quantization trade-offs: 4-bit gives big memory and throughput wins but can increase hallucination risk on very low-temperature settings — recommend one eval prompt-set before production rollout. Int8 is a safer middle ground for semantic fidelity.
- Batching: aim for median batch of 6 with a cap at 12; we enforce a soft latency SLO at runtime and drop batch growth once tail latency exceeds threshold.
- Cache: for chat with repeated system/prefix text, a 20–30% KV cache hit is realistic; allocate ~4–8GB KV per GPU for your median convo volume.

I attached the short notes (quant-recommendation-notes.pdf). We can add a small benchmark table if you share a representative prompt set and target p95.
